Moja Time Clock & Approval Process

Standard Operating Procedure — High-Level Overview & Process Flow

1. System Overview

The Moja time tracking system is a PIN-based kiosk time clock with bi-weekly timecard generation and a two-tier approval workflow (employee review, then admin approval).

Key Design Principles

  • No employee login required — staff use 4-digit PINs to clock in/out; timecard review uses emailed token links
  • Bi-weekly pay periods — Saturday through Friday (two-week cycles)
  • Two break types — "Break" (paid, not deducted) and "Lunch" (unpaid, deducted from total hours)
  • Auto clock-out — shifts exceeding 16 hours are automatically closed
  • Rate limiting — 5 failed PIN attempts per IP address per 15 minutes
  • Overtime — calculated per week at 40-hour threshold (configurable)

2. Daily Clock In/Out Process

Steps:

  1. Employee approaches the kiosk and enters their 4-digit PIN
  2. System validates PIN (bcrypt comparison) and displays employee name and status
  3. Employee taps Clock In, Clock Out, or Break as appropriate
  4. Screen auto-resets after 45 seconds of inactivity
Employee enters PIN │ PIN validated via edge function (bcrypt) │ ┌─────────────────┬───────────────────┬──────────────────┐ │ │ │ [CLOCK IN] [BREAK] [CLOCK OUT] │ │ │ New shift record Break log created Shift closed with created (paid or lunch) duration calculated │ │ │ Staff marked Staff marked Staff marked "clocked in" "on break" "clocked out"

Automatic Safeguards:

ScenarioSystem Behavior
Employee clocks out while on breakBreak is auto-ended, then shift closes
Shift exceeds 16 hoursAuto clock-out triggered; duration capped
Employee clocks in with stale open shiftStale shift auto-closed, new shift begins
5+ failed PIN attempts from same IPBlocked for 15 minutes

3. Break Handling

Break TypePaid?Deducted from Hours?Typical Duration
Break (Regular)YesNo15 minutes
LunchNoYes30 minutes
Note: Only lunch breaks reduce an employee's total paid hours. Regular (paid) breaks are tracked but do not affect the timecard total.

4. Timecard Generation

When:

  • Automatically — Friday evening via scheduled cron job
  • Manually — Admin can trigger generation at any time

What Happens:

  1. Pay period is created or located (Saturday–Friday, bi-weekly)
  2. For each active employee:
    • All shift durations in the period are summed (gross minutes)
    • Lunch break minutes are deducted
    • Overtime calculated per week (hours exceeding 40h threshold)
    • Timecard report created with status PENDING REVIEW
  3. Email sent to each employee with:
    • Total hours summary
    • Detailed shift table
    • Review link (token-based, no login needed)
    • Deadline: 8:00 PM EST Friday
Friday Evening (Cron or Manual Trigger) │ Sum all clock_logs for pay period per employee │ Deduct lunch break minutes │ Calculate weekly overtime (40h threshold) │ Generate timecard_reports (status: pending_review) │ Email employees with review link + deadline

5. Employee Review Phase

Employees receive an email with a unique link to review their timecard. No login is required.

Employee ActionResult
Approve timecardStatus → EMPLOYEE APPROVED
Add a note to a shiftStatus → HAS NOTES
Submit a correction (new times/hours)Correction created as "pending"; status → HAS NOTES
Add a missing shiftCreates pending correction for the day
No action by 8:00 PM FridayAuto-approved → EMPLOYEE APPROVED

6. Admin Approval Phase

After employee review, admins finalize timecards in the admin dashboard.

Admin ActionResult
Resolve employee notesIf all resolved → status reverts to PENDING REVIEW
Approve employee correctionHours recalculated with corrected times
Reject employee correctionOriginal times kept; rejection reason stored
Admin edits shift directlyAuto-approved correction; hours recalculated immediately
Admin adds missing shiftNew shift created with auto-approved correction
Final approvalStatus → APPROVED; "Hours Confirmed" email sent to employee

7. Complete Status Lifecycle

┌─────────────────┐ │ PENDING REVIEW │ (Generated, awaiting employee) └───────┬─────────┘ │ ├─── Employee adds notes/corrections │ │ │ ┌─────┴───────────┐ │ │ HAS NOTES │ (Needs admin attention) │ └──────┬──────────┘ │ │ │ ├─── Admin resolves all notes │ │ │ │ │ └───→ Back to PENDING REVIEW │ │ ├─── Employee approves (or auto-approve at 8PM) │ ┌─────┴─────────────────┐ │ EMPLOYEE APPROVED │ (Awaiting admin final sign-off) └──────┬──────────────────┘ │ ├─── Admin approves │ ┌─────┴─────────────────┐ │ APPROVED │ (Final — confirmation email sent) └────────────────────────┘

8. Correction Requests Flow

Employee-Initiated Corrections:

  1. Employee opens timecard via emailed link
  2. Clicks a shift and proposes changes (new in/out times or total hours)
  3. System creates correction with status PENDING
  4. Timecard status changes to "Has Notes" for admin visibility
  5. Admin reviews and either approves (hours recalculated) or rejects (reason stored)

Admin-Initiated Corrections:

  1. Admin edits shift directly from the review dashboard
  2. Correction is created with status APPROVED immediately
  3. Total hours are recalculated on the spot
Hours Recalculation Logic: For each shift, if an approved correction exists, its proposed duration is used instead of the original. Total lunch minutes are then deducted from the sum. Net hours = (sum of effective gross minutes - total lunch minutes) / 60.
